text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All is now set for local council election on Saturday, the first step to full democracy next year; some 55.7 million voters registered to vote.
- Oil workers union PENGASSAN members stopped 300 staff of Elf Petroleum Nigeria Limited going into work in a strike to demand implementation of new remuneration package.
- Wildlife damages electricity line causing power failure nationwide for about eight hours.
- Canada finally closes its embassy in Nigeria following similar action by Nigeria last year.

- Visiting African human rights team meets mother of hanged minority rights activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and 19 youths from the Ogoni tribe who are being detained over the murder of four chiefs for which the activist and eight others were executed.
- Demand for foreign exchange at weekly auction falls as local naira currency depreciates.
- Government approves trip by cashew exporters to India.
- Vision 2010 committee planning Nigeria's economic future favours privatisation of loss-making state enterprises, says member Isaac Aluko-Olokun.
- Exiled wing of the opposition group NADECO meets in the United States and Britain over the trial of their key members who were charged this week with treason for recent bomb blasts in the country.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha pleads for peaceful local council election on Saturday.
- Central bank reminds distressed banks that they face liquidation after March 31 if they do not recapitalise.
